headline: Menzies edges Raymond Smith 5-4 at the Grand Slam and discusses weight loss
standfirst: Cameron Menzies won a deciding leg against Raymond Smith in Wolverhampton and now faces Stephen Bunting in a straight shootout.
body: Cameron Menzies beat Raymond Smith 5-4 in his opening Grand Slam of Darts match on Sunday afternoon, setting up a group decider with Stephen Bunting.

Menzies was unimpressed with his own display. He said he had started badly, called the first leg "stinking", and felt he had stolen the win, according to Dartsnews. He was generous about Smith, noting that the Australian had been one game from a Tour Card and was proof that players without cards can compete at this level.

The Scot also spoke about a marked change in his appearance. Dartsnews reported that he has lost a large amount of weight, taking up walking and jogging after earlier warning signs, including a moment on a flight that made him face the reality of his condition.
He described himself as a chronic overthinker, saying the mental side of the game is harder for him than the scoring. He joked that he would be giving Bunting "a few jabs" before they meet.
With only the winner of each three-player group advancing, Monday's meeting with Bunting is effectively a knockout tie for a place in the last 16.

sources.name: Dartsnews
sources.title: "I didn't actually know how bad I was": Cameron Menzies loses nearly five stone in weight after wake-up call on flight sees stark reality
